title: Data Exposure
intro: Data Exposure controls which additional table columns the dashboard builder offers. Administrators use it to hide columns or approve their availability. You need Manage data exposure.

This policy covers additional table columns in the dashboard builder. Built-in dimensions, raw SQL and connector-backed reports are outside it. Hiding a column here does not erase its data or remove database access.
The PII badge means personally identifiable information. Showing one of these columns requires an extra confirmation, then Save.
Use your own approved column policy. The pictures use an isolated test installation and restore the demonstrated columns afterward. No sample records are required.

tasks.title: Hide an additional dashboard column
intro: Use this when an additional column should no longer be offered in the dashboard builder.
steps: Open your user menu at the bottom left, choose Settings, then select Data Exposure.
Find the table containing the column. The example uses Patient. Match both the table and column name.
Read Shown or Hidden beside the switch. The example starts with managing_organization Shown.
Turn off its switch. The draft now says Hidden.
Unsaved changes means the draft has not yet changed the stored policy.
Open the page dots at the top right and select Save.
tasks.result: The indicator clears. The saved column remains Hidden after reopening the page and is absent from additional builder columns.

tasks.title: Discard unsaved policy changes
intro: Use this when you want to keep the saved policy after changing a switch.
steps: Check which switch you changed. The example has turned the hidden column back on without saving.
Open the page dots and select Discard.
tasks.result: The page reloads the saved policy. The unsaved switch change disappears.

tasks.title: Approve showing a personally identifying column
intro: Use this only after deciding that dashboard users should be able to use this additional column. The pictures use a test installation.
steps: Find the correct table and column. The example is surname in Patient, marked PII and Hidden.
Turn the switch on. Read the warning, then select Un-hide to approve the draft. Select Cancel to leave it hidden.
The column now says Shown. The policy still has unsaved changes.
Open the page dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The saved column is available among additional dashboard-builder columns.

tasks.title: Hide a personally identifying column again
intro: Use this when an approved identifying column should no longer be offered.
steps: Find the column and turn off its switch. The example hides surname again.
Open the page dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The column is Hidden in the saved policy. No identifying data was deleted.

tasks.title: Show a column without a PII warning
intro: Use this when a non-PII additional column should be available again.
steps: Find the correct column and turn on its switch. The example restores managing_organization.
Open the page dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The saved column is available among additional dashboard-builder columns again.

tasks.title: Review the policy on a phone
intro: Use the same table groups and switches on a phone. Scroll vertically through the groups.
steps: Find the correct group before changing a column.
Check its name, any PII badge, and Shown or Hidden state before changing the switch. Save changes through the page dots.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: Use a test installation. Hide a non-PII column, save, then restore it. Try Discard with an unsaved switch change. Only practise PII approval with fictional data and restore the intended policy afterward.

end.title: Limits
paragraphs: This is not a database security boundary or a data-deletion tool. Built-in dimensions, raw SQL and connector-backed reports are outside this policy. Column changes remain drafts until Save.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: The policy did not change. Check Unsaved changes, then choose Save in the page dots.
Discard is unavailable. No unsaved switch change exists.
A hidden field remains available elsewhere. Check whether it is a built-in dimension, raw SQL field or connector-backed report field, which this policy does not govern.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Read Dashboards for building widgets and Roles for permissions. Read Start here for command-line setup.
